August 10, 2026

Trump reportedly willing to end Iran war without a nuclear deal

tags: war, politics, foreign-policy
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @hunteralexanderhowell

According to the Wall Street Journal, President Trump has told senior officials he is prepared to end the US military campaign against Iran without any agreement on Iran's nuclear program, seeking only the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. That marks a reversal from earlier positions demanding Iran's unconditional surrender and a deal replacing the Obama-era nuclear agreement. The Strait of Hormuz was open before the US strikes began and has since been closed by Iran. Reporting indicates Trump privately described the war as lost, with a plan to return to roughly pre-war conditions; polling cited from Ipsos shows a majority of US taxpayers oppose the campaign.

Iran says it will not negotiate until after Trump leaves office

tags: politics, war, foreign-policy
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iranian officials stated they will not negotiate with President Trump or his administration. They said talks would resume only in January 2029, when the current administration concludes.

Capital One closed more than 300 accounts linked to Trump over money laundering concerns

tags: legal, markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Capital One shut down over 300 accounts tied to President Trump and his businesses, citing potential violations of the Anti-Money Laundering Act after identifying suspicious transactions. The accounts spanned the Trump Organization, Eric Trump, Trump-branded wine and water products, and a golf course developer. The closures drew limited news coverage.

Republicans attack Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed over his marriage and faith

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

President Trump posted a comparison of "two different versions of America" contrasting himself and Melania Trump with Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and his wife. El-Sayed responded that the contrast was between people who make billions off the public and a couple who genuinely love each other and want to build a country where families can thrive. Separately, Senator Tommy Tuberville called El-Sayed a "terrorist" and a "radical Islamist" after Michigan Democrats nominated him. El-Sayed is a Detroit-born Rhodes Scholar with two doctorates who served as Detroit's health director at 30 and taught epidemiology at Columbia University.

Zelenskiy says up to 50,000 North Korean troops could deploy to Russia

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said as many as 50,000 North Korean troops could be deployed to Russia. The statement points to a deepening military relationship between Moscow and Pyongyang.

Poland and Baltic states brace for possible Russian false-flag attack

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Poland and the Baltic states are tightening security amid concerns that Russia could stage a false-flag attack. Authorities in the region have raised their posture in response.

Russia says Ukrainian drone attack killed 13 in Nizhnekamsk

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia said 13 people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan. Ukraine said it had struck an oil refinery there.

Transportation Department recruits video gamers as air traffic controllers

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the department has escalated a hiring campaign, launched in April, that recruits video gamers into air traffic controller positions. He said the effort reached 94% of its hiring goal in the fastest time on record, with more than 2,000 new controllers hired and candidates reaching the academy faster than any previous class. The advertising campaign specifically featured Fortnite among the games used to target recruits.

Seven dead from flesh-eating bacteria in Gulf states as officials link cases to warming waters

tags: health, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

Seven people have died from flesh-eating bacteria in Gulf states in recent weeks, five in Louisiana and two in Florida. Louisiana has recorded nine cases, roughly four times its average, and state health officials issued a warning urging precautions. Officials said the bacterium becomes more prevalent as coastal waters warm, a trend tied to rising global temperatures.

Taylor Farms recalls salsa and guacamole nationwide amid salmonella outbreak

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

Taylor Farms recalled salsa, guacamole and other prepared foods containing jalapenos sold at Walmart, Kroger, Whole Foods, Target, Trader Joe's and Hannaford across roughly 20 states. The CDC reports a salmonella outbreak that has sickened about 345 people and led to about 36 hospitalizations. Chipotle and Qdoba have pulled jalapenos from their menus. The action follows a separate Taylor Farms recall of shredded lettuce.

Islamophobic harassment campaigns spread online, including a planned pig release in Dearborn

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A wave of anti-Muslim content has circulated online, much of it centered on pork as a taunt directed at Muslims. A video showed a woman describing ordering pork after a woman in hijab sat near her, and a man in Alabama publicised plans to release pigs in Dearborn, Michigan, a city with a Muslim population of about 54%. Police were called and the pig release was called off.

New bruising on Trump's forearm renews questions about his health

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

A Reuters image shows multiple pronounced bruises running up President Trump's forearm, extending beyond the bruising previously visible on the back of his hands. Trump has also been diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency, which has caused swollen ankles. The White House medical office has not provided full disclosure about the health of the president, who has turned 80.

CNN review finds Patriot Games competitors selected for political loyalty

tags: politics, sports
sources: @aaronparnas

The Patriot Games, an athletic competition featuring one high school boy and one girl from each of the 50 states, opened in Ohio. A CNN review found competitors were chosen based on loyalty to the MAGA movement rather than athletic ability, with many aged 14 to 17, predominantly white, and drawn from homeschooling or Christian private academies. Several do not live in the states they represent, including a boy representing Puerto Rico who is from Texas and a girl representing Massachusetts who attends school in California. Organisers told competitors of only one event, the 100-meter dash, in advance.

White House produces Game of Thrones-themed video with taxpayer funds

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The White House released a taxpayer-funded video using Game of Thrones imagery to depict President Trump on the Iron Throne, claiming he has restored the nation's capital. The video omits the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, which remains in disrepair.
